```{r setup}
#| include: false

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)

# ---- EDIT THIS: path to your data file ------------------------------------
# Put the CSV next to this .qmd file (or give a full path).
# data_path <- "capstone_data - Sheet1 (7).csv"

# Person whose row label is bolded in every heatmap
highlight_person <- "Librarian_Me"

# Person excluded from the activity heatmaps
exclude_person <- "Librarian_RC"

# Involvement levels (ordinal: RARE < TOUCH < DO)
level_order  <- c("RARE", "TOUCH", "DO")
level_colors <- c("RARE" = "#fee5d9", "TOUCH" = "#fb6a4a", "DO" = "#a50f15")
```

## Overview

- **Goal:** understand how staff time and responsibilities are distributed across the university
- **Data:** capstone worksheet, tidy spreadsheet
- **Approach:** R + tidyverse + ggplot2 with the help of Claude.ai Sonnet 5.5 Medium

## What is an R2? 
- Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education
  - R2s are "Doctoral Universities: High Research Activity"
  - That confer at least 20 doctorates but fewer than 70
  - At least $5 million in R&D (R1 threshold is at least $50 million)
  
## Wichita State University Libraries
<!-- Image from a web URL -->
![Reclining Figure (Hand) by Henry Moore](https://www.wichita.edu/about/wsunews/news/2022/04-april/_images/sculptures_ablah_1200.jpg){width=33%}
  
  - Main Library and Music & Fine Arts Library
  
  - Research and Instructional Services, Tech Services, and Access Services Librarians
  
## Personnel Titles

- 9 Librarians with functional titles and subject area liaisonhips
- 1 Library staff with patent and copyright expertise
- 2 Technical services librarians
- 2 Faculty in mathematics, statistics, and physics

## Roadmap

1.  Percentage of time allocated by person
2.  Involvement heatmaps by stage of the data life cycle
    - Collecting and discovery
    - Exploration and analysis
    - Publishing and preserving
3.  Involvement by data type

::: notes
Load and Prepare the Data

```{r load-data}
#| echo: false

df <- read_csv("T:/JungMee/ICPSR_data/Providing_data_services/ICPSR Capstone/capstone_data - Sheet1 (7).csv", skip = 2)

# Refer to the first two columns by position (robust to header changes):
#   x = person's title, y = percentage of work hours
y_col <- names(df)[2]
df <- df %>% rename(x = 1, y = 2)


```


The first two rows of the sheet are skipped. Columns 1 and 2 are renamed by position so the code still works if the header text changes.
:::

## Percentage Time Allocated by Person

```{r bar-chart}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

p_bar <- ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(x, -y), y = y, fill = y)) +
  geom_col(color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(y, "%")),
            vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = y_col, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage Time Allocated by Person",
    x = "Title of Person",
    y = "Percentage of Work Hours"
  ) +
  ylim(0, max(df$y) * 1.15) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p_bar
```

## How to Interpret the Heatmaps

Each activity is rated on an ordinal scale:

| Level | Meaning | Colour |
|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **RARE** | Rarely involved | [ ]{style="background:#fee5d9;padding:2px 12px;"} |
| **TOUCH** | Touches the work sometimes | [ ]{style="background:#fb6a4a;padding:2px 12px;"} |
| **DO** | Does the work | [ ]{style="background:#a50f15;padding:2px 12px;"} |

The row label for **`Librarian_Me`** is shown in bold to highlight it.

::: notes
A Reusable Heatmap Function

The same reshape-and-plot steps repeat for each section, so they are wrapped in one function.

```{r heatmap-fn}
#| echo: true

my_order <- c("Librarian_Me", "Librarian_AB", "Librarian_FH", "Librarian_GW", "Librarian_MK", "Librarian_RC", "Librarian_SM", "Librarian_SR", "Librarian_SW", "Professor_TF", "Professor_YK", "Staff_JP" 
            )

df <- df %>%
  mutate(x = factor(x, levels = my_order))

make_heatmap <- function(data, prefix, title, exclude = NULL, person_order = NULL) {

  d <- data
  if (!is.null(exclude)) d <- filter(d, x != exclude)

  # use your order if given, otherwise the order in the data
  lv <- if (is.null(person_order)) unique(as.character(d$x)) else
        person_order[person_order %in% d$x]

  plot_df <- d %>%
    select(x, starts_with(prefix)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-x, names_to = "Activity", values_to = "Level") %>%
    mutate(
      Activity = str_remove(Activity, fixed(prefix)),
      Level    = factor(Level, levels = level_order, ordered = TRUE),
      Person   = factor(x, levels = lv)            # <- was unique(x)
    )

  person_levels <- levels(plot_df$Person)          # <- uncommented
  faces  <- ifelse(person_levels == highlight_person, "bold", "plain")
  colors <- ifelse(person_levels == highlight_person, "black", "darkgrey")

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Activity, y = Person, fill = Level)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = level_colors, name = "Involvement") +
    labs(title = title, x = "Activity", y = "Person") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = faces, colour = colors),
      panel.grid  = element_blank(),
      plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}
```
:::

## Collecting and Discovery

```{r heatmap-collecting}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

p_heatmap <- make_heatmap(
  df,
  prefix  = "Collecting and discovery_",
  title   = "Collecting and Discovery: Involvement by Person",
  exclude = exclude_person
)
p_heatmap
```

## Key Takeaways

- *At a smaller R2 institution, the solo data librarian is involved in many stages of the data life cycle*
- *Informing subject area librarians of key data resources helped those needing to find data*
- *As `Librarian_Me` establishes the position, I am identifying a strong preference for teaching data analysis skills* 
- *A growing need to geo-spatial data and visual data has emerged*
- *Greater across campus partnerships with Office of Research and Data Governance has developed*
